best_for: Thunderbird users on Windows or Linux who want extras like multi-line message lists, vertical tabs or a Linux tray icon, and who are happy to stay on the slower ESR release line.

points.title: Thunderbird with extras
points.text: Betterbird is a soft fork of Thunderbird that adds its own features and fixes. Examples are a multi-line message list, vertical tabs, account colors, regex search, search inside encrypted mail and a system tray icon on Linux.

points.title: Try it on your current profile
points.text: Betterbird follows Thunderbird's ESR version numbers, so it can run side by side with the matching Thunderbird release and open the same profile. If you do not like it, you can switch back without rebuilding your mail setup.

points.title: Most add-ons still work
points.text: The project says about 98% of Thunderbird add-ons run in Betterbird, installed from addons.thunderbird.net as usual. Add-ons without a compatible version are blocked, and the Add-ons Manager tells you which.

points.title: Old series are unsafe
points.text: Betterbird tracks Thunderbird's extended support line. The 115, 128 and 140 series have reached end of life, and the project warns against them because of unpatched security holes. Stay on the current series.

points.title: Free under MPL 2.0, donations welcome
points.text: Betterbird is open source under the Mozilla Public License 2.0. The project asks for donations and has a small shop. Language packs cover German, French, Spanish, Japanese and nine other languages, with more on request.

points.title: What this site lists
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 2 versions of the machine-wide installer; the project also offers a portable zip. Linux lists one verified Flathub build for x64 and Arm64. Mac builds exist on betterbird.eu but are not listed here and are not notarized, so macOS needs a manual step to open them. Release 153.8.0esr-bb14 came out on November 21, 2026.
